title: Karkain native compilation path -- qualified feature matrix
scope: The Karkain-owned native path (kcc), i.e. `karkain build --target native-x86_64-<os>` with NO C compiler and NO Go toolchain in the program-compilation path. This is the v1.2.0 'Sovereignty I' qualification surface. It is NOT the C-backend path and NOT the WASM path.

statuses.supported: Lowered by the self-hosted driver, with a passing gate that executes or byte-compares it.
statuses.implemented_not_gated: Lowered by the driver, but no gate exercises the kcc side of it yet. Not advertised as supported.
statuses.not_supported: Refused BY NAME with a diagnostic and no image. Never silently mis-lowered.
statuses.blocked: Blocked by a known architectural dependency outside this path.

features.construct: call to a user function with arguments
return value from a user function
array element read with a VARIABLE index
array element read with an ARITHMETIC index
array iteration in a C-style `for` loop
array element inside an arithmetic expression
array element passed to a function
nested array access (an index that is itself an element read)

features.note: A runtime error with a non-zero exit and no value printed. The diagnostic text goes to stderr, which the Phase-152-B0 GetStdHandle limitation leaves empty on this host, so the exit status is the observable.

features.construct: array index that is not an integer expression
array element of a non-int type
features.note: Array elements are int literals only.

features.construct: native frame layout (the frame-size immediate) matches the Go oracle's
features.note: The frame-size immediate is read out of each generated image and compared with the oracle's, for both targets. The Linux target matters because the Windows 16-byte rounding quantises an 8-byte difference away.

features.construct: the map-stage frame unit is reserved program-wide
the string-stage frame unit is reserved program-wide
features.note: The oracle reserves it program-wide over five operations; the driver reserves it per function over two. Measured 640 bytes against 3200. Pinned as a known divergence by TestPhaseNATFrame_TheStringStageIsStillDivergent.
The driver lowers maps (natMapFind/natMapSet/natMapGet) and the Go oracle gates them in pkg/native/phase150b3c_test.go, but no gate exercises the kcc side of the map path yet.

features.construct: string binding inside a loop body
features.note: The rodata cursor is threaded per statement list in this driver.
The arena is sized at compile time on the assumption that each allocation site runs at most once.
Same arena bound as the row above.
The subset has no `if`, so a recursive function cannot terminate: both engines stack-overflow identically. Parity, not support.
The native path has no stdlib runtime: `import std.*` is refused by the driver. This is closure condition 2 of v1.2.0, carried to v1.3.0 as UNMET.
Closure condition 3 of v1.2.0, carried to v1.3.0 as UNMET.
The native path has no concurrency runtime.

independence_evidence.claim: The qualified native path does not invoke a C compiler, a C source generator, the Go compiler or the Go runtime.
independence_evidence.how: pkg/cli/phase151h_qualification_test.go installs PATH shims for `gcc` and `go` that log every invocation, warms the self-hosted compiler OUTSIDE the trace, and then builds a program natively with the shims on PATH. An empty log is the evidence.

known_limitations: The self-hosted driver has no register allocator, so a function with five or more simultaneously-live int locals AND control flow is encoded differently from the Go oracle (which has the Phase-150C allocator). The difference is an encoding strategy, not a wrong answer; the boundary is pinned by TestPhaseNATIf_TheRegisterAllocatorBoundaryIsPinned.
The rodata cursor is threaded per statement list in the driver, so a STRING literal inside a branch or a loop body is refused. An integer binding inside a branch or a loop body is supported.

A program with an array is NOT byte-identical to the Go oracle: TWO bytes differ, the absolute rodata addresses of the runtime-error reporter's strings, because the two engines intern them in a different ORDER (the oracle emits the reporter helper before the user function, so its strings are interned first; the driver appends them after the program's own literals). The FRAME itself matches the oracle exactly -- the 8-byte difference NAT-FRAME closed was an unreserved map-stage slot, not a rounding rule. Array programs are therefore compared BEHAVIOURALLY, against the C backend.

The STRING stage is reserved PROGRAM-WIDE by the Go oracle (over five operations: concat, string equality, string slicing, push and a string field assignment) but PER FUNCTION by the self-hosted driver (over two: concat sites and push counts). So a program that assigns a string to a field gets no string stage at all, and a program whose string work happens in one function gets a different frame in another. Measured: 640 bytes against 3200, a difference of exactly 2560 (the string stage, 8 * 5 * maxBinDepth). Pinned by TestPhaseNATFrame_TheStringStageIsStillDivergent.
`while` and the C-style `for` are lowered; `for ... in`, `break` and `continue` OUTSIDE a loop, and the arena-using constructs inside a loop are refused by name.

The heap arena is sized at compile time on the assumption that each allocation site runs at most once, so a string concatenation, a `push()` or a map insertion inside a loop is refused. No iteration-scoped arena checkpoint exists, because proving that no live reference escapes an iteration is a separate analysis.
A comparison is a CONDITION, not a value: `let c = (a < b)` is refused.
KIR is verified by the compiler on the default check path but is NOT the backend's input. The native driver consumes the AST directly. Wiring KIR into the backend is not done.
